title_en: American Airlines Takes Delivery Of 4 New Airbus A321neos In One Week
title_zh: 美国航空一周内接收 4 架新空客 A321neo
summary: American Airlines has received four new Airbus jets in one week as its A321neo and A321XLR fleets expand.
summary_zh: 随着 A321neo 和 A321XLR 机队的扩大，美国航空在一周内接收了四架新的空客飞机。
body_en: American Airlines Takes Delivery Of 4 New Airbus A321neos In One Week

Paul has had a career of 25+ years focused on the international technology sector, which has taken him to over 100 countries. Along the way, he developed a deep love for aviation, with a travel bucket list measured by aircraft types flown rather than destinations reached. Now he brings that avgeek passion, along with the journalism experience he accumulated early in his career, to write insightful pieces for Simple Flying.

American Airlines is accelerating its fleet modernization, taking delivery of four new Airbus aircraft in just seven days. The arrivals comprise three A321neos and one A321XLR , with the latter, registered N311NY, scheduled to arrive on Friday, according to Thomas Beam . The deliveries expand American's narrowbody fleet as the carrier prepares for further domestic and international growth.

The airline expects another four Airbus deliveries before the end of 2026, including three A321neos and an additional A321XLR. No additional Boeing aircraft are scheduled to arrive this year, making Airbus the sole supplier of new mainline jets during the final weeks of 2026. Interestingly, despite their visual similarities, the two A321 variants serve distinctly different roles within American's network.
American's Airbus Deliveries Accelerate In October

The latest arrivals highlight the pace of American's narrowbody expansion. Flightradar24 shows that N311NY, an A321XLR built in Hamburg, touched down on its delivery flight to Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), and joins three standard A321neos delivered earlier this week.

American's latest financial disclosures reveal the scale of its fleet renewal. As of September 30, the airline still had 165 Airbus A320-family aircraft on order, including seven scheduled for the remainder of 2026. That schedule has clearly been advanced because even with this week's four arrivals, the latest delivery information indicates four more Airbus deliveries expected before year-end, with three A321neos and an additional XLR.

The deliveries have also taken American to an important milestone, as it now has 100 of the next-generation A321s in operation, alongside its 218 A321-200s. Of those, 11 are XLRs, allowing the carrier to invest in new long-haul destinations, a fact highlighted by American's former SVP of Network Planning, Brian Znotins in the carrier's 2027 international expansion

"The A321XLR is transforming our international network, expanding it to offer destinations to satisfy every travel palate. Combined with our investments enhancing our onboard product and inflight experience, travelers have more reasons to choose American when they fly around the world."
The A321XLR Is Transforming American's International Network

American received its first A321XLR in October 2025 , becoming the first US operator of the type. Its original 50-aircraft commitment was subsequently reduced to 40, including five delivered by the end of 2025. Each aircraft features 20 Flagship Suite business class seats, 12 premium economy seats, and 123 economy seats, emphasizing premium revenue rather than maximum capacity.

The XLR restores some of the long-range narrowbody capability American lost when it retired its Boeing 757s in 2020. Its economics make thinner transatlantic routes viable without deploying a much larger Boeing 787 Dreamliner. The aircraft initially entered service on premium transcontinental flights, before expanding into international markets as more aircraft became available.

American's 2027 schedule demonstrates its ambitions, with four additional European routes assigned to the XLR. Philadelphia–Vienna, measuring approximately 4,321 miles (6,955 km), is particularly notable as it will become the world's longest narrowbody flight . The route will operate daily from May 6 through January 2028, while New York gains new services to Amsterdam and Nice.
The A321neo Powers American's Domestic Expansion

The standard A321neo remains the backbone of American's next-generation, high-capacity narrowbody strategy. Fleet records show it now has 89 of the type in the fleet and firm orders for a further 127 frames. It expects to receive an additional 27 A321-family aircraft in 2027, but the split between A321neos and A321XLRs has not been announced.

Configured with 196 seats, including 20 First Class and 47 Main Cabin Extra seats, American's legacy A321neos accommodate 41 more passengers than the XLR. It is particularly valuable on busy domestic routes connecting American's major hubs and supports the gradual replacement of older narrowbodies. Its versatility extends internationally, with Philadelphia–Reykjavík scheduled to launch in May 2027.

American's 737 MAX 8s complement the A321neos, offering 172 seats on routes requiring less capacity. The airline also has 115 Boeing 737-family aircraft on order, including the larger MAX 10, although deliveries are not scheduled to begin until 2029 (or later). Until then, Airbus narrowbodies will lead the expansion of the American Airlines network, both domestically and increasingly on new transatlantic routes.
body_zh: 美国航空一周内接收 4 架新空客 A321neo
Paul 拥有超过 25 年的职业生涯，专注于国际技术领域，足迹遍及 100 多个国家。一路走来，他对航空产生了深深的热爱，他的旅行愿望清单是根据飞行的飞机类型而不是到达的目的地来衡量的。现在，他带着这种平均极客的热情，以及他在职业生涯早期积累的新闻经验，为《简单飞行》撰写了富有洞察力的文章。
美国航空正在加速其机队现代化，在短短 7 天内接收了四架新的空客飞机。据 Thomas Beam 称，抵达的飞机包括三架 A321neo 和一架 A321XLR，后者注册号为 N311NY，计划于周五抵达。随着美国航空为进一步的国内和国际增长做准备，这些交付扩大了美国航空的窄体机机队。
该航空公司预计在 2026 年底前再交付四架空客飞机，其中包括三架 A321neo 和另外一架 A321XLR。今年预计不会有更多波音飞机抵达，这使得空中客车公司成为 2026 年最后几周新型干线喷气式飞机的唯一供应商。有趣的是，尽管这两种 A321 机型在外观上相似，但它们在美国航空网络中扮演着截然不同的角色。
美国航空 10 月份空中客车交付量加速
最新抵达的飞机凸显了美国航空窄体飞机扩张的步伐。 Flightradar24 显示，N311NY（一架在汉堡制造的 A321XLR）已在飞往达拉斯/沃斯堡国际机场 (DFW) 的交付航班上着陆，并加入本周早些时候交付的三架标准 A321neo 行列。
美国航空最新的财务披露揭示了其机队更新的规模。截至 9 月 30 日，该航空公司仍有 165 架空客 A320 系列飞机订购，其中 7 架计划在 2026 年剩余时间内交付。该计划显然已经提前，因为即使本周有 4 架飞机抵达，最新交付信息显示，预计年底前还将交付 4 架空客飞机，其中包括 3 架 A321neo 和一架 XLR。
这些交付也使美国航空达到了一个重要的里程碑，因为该公司目前拥有 100 架下一代 A321 飞机以及 218 架 A321-200 飞机。其中 11 个是 XLR，使该航空公司能够投资新的长途目的地，美国航空前网络规划高级副总裁 Brian Znotins 在该航空公司 2027 年国际扩张中强调了这一事实
“A321XLR 正在改变我们的国际网络，将其扩展为提供满足各种旅行口味的目的地。结合我们对增强机上产品和机上体验的投资，旅客在环游世界时有更多理由选择美国航空。”
A321XLR 正在改变美国航空的国际网络
美国航空于 2025 年 10 月接收了第一架 A321XLR，成为美国第一家该类型运营商。其最初的 50 架飞机承诺随后减少到 40 架，其中 5 架将于 2025 年底交付。每架飞机均设有 20 个旗舰套房商务舱座位、12 个高级经济舱座位和 123 个经济舱座位，强调溢价收入而不是最大运力。
XLR 恢复了美国航空在 2020 年退役波音 757 时失去的部分远程窄体飞机能力。其经济性使更窄的跨大西洋航线变得可行，而无需部署更大的波音 787 梦想飞机。该飞机最初在高级跨大陆航班上投入使用，随后随着更多飞机的出现而扩展到国际市场。
美国航空 2027 年的时间表展示了其雄心，新增 4 条欧洲航线分配给 XLR。费城-维也纳航线全长约 4,321 英里（6,955 公里），尤其引人注目，因为它将成为世界上最长的窄体航班。该航线将于 5 月 6 日至 2028 年 1 月期间每天运营，同时纽约将新增飞往阿姆斯特丹和尼斯的航班。
A321neo 为美国航空的国内扩张提供动力
标准 A321neo 仍然是美国航空下一代大容量窄体机战略的支柱。机队记录显示，该机队目前拥有 89 架该型号飞机，并确定另外 127 架的订单。预计到 2027 年将再接收 27 架 A321 系列飞机，但 A321neos 和 A321XLR 之间的分配尚未公布。
美国航空的传统 A321neos 配备 196 个座位，其中包括 20 个头等舱座位和 47 个主舱额外座位，比 XLR 多容纳 41 名乘客。它在连接美国主要枢纽的繁忙国内航线上尤其有价值，并支持逐步更换旧的窄体飞机。其多功能性已扩展到国际范围，计划于 2027 年 5 月开通费城-雷克雅未克航线。
美国航空 737 MAX 8 是对 A321neos 的补充，在运力需求较少的航线上提供 172 个座位。该航空公司还订购了 115 架波音 737 系列飞机，其中包括较大的 MAX 10，不过预计要到 2029 年（或更晚）才会开始交付。在那之前，空客窄体机将引领美国航空网络的扩张，无论是国内航线还是越来越多的新的跨大西洋航线。

title_en: Iberia adds 98 Andalusia flights following rail accident, caps Economy fares at €99
title_zh: 铁路事故后，Iberia 增加了 98 趟安达卢西亚航班，经济舱票价上限为 99 欧元
summary: Iberia and Iberia Express have scheduled 98 additional flights between Madrid and Andalusia through 8 November, responding to increased demand following the rail accident in Urda, Toledo. The airlines say they have added 20,718 seats, increasing capacity by 93
summary_zh: Iberia 和 Iberia Express 已计划在 11 月 8 日之前在马德里和安达卢西亚之间增加 98 趟航班，以满足随后增加的需求。
body_en: Iberia adds 98 Andalusia flights following rail accident, caps Economy fares at €99 - Aviation24.be
Home International Airlines Group (IAG) Iberia Iberia adds 98 Andalusia flights following rail accident, caps Economy fares at...
Iberia and Iberia Express have scheduled 98 additional flights between Madrid and Andalusia through 8 November, responding to increased demand following the rail accident in Urda , Toledo.

The airlines say they have added 20,718 seats, increasing capacity by 93% against the original schedule. Madrid–Seville accounts for 10,734 extra seats and Madrid–Málaga for 9,984. Iberia will operate 78 of the additional flights, and Iberia Express will operate the remaining 20.

For the All Saints’ Day holiday period through Monday, the group has scheduled 34 extra flights and 7,642 additional seats across the two routes. The airline is also deploying larger aircraft on selected existing services.

Until 8 November, fares between Madrid and Andalusia are capped at €99 per one-way segment in Economy and €149 in Business. Booking flexibility is available for passengers affected by the rail accident. Iberia is also working on additional flights from 9 November, although these have not yet been scheduled.

body_en: Four reported dead after Italian EUFOR Chinook crashes in Bosnia - Aviation24.be
Home Boeing Boeing Defense Four reported dead after Italian EUFOR Chinook crashes in Bosnia

Four military personnel have reportedly died and 11 others were injured after an Italian Army Boeing CH-47 Chinook operating with EUFOR Althea crashed near Gorica, in Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Br?ko district, on 29 October 2026.
EUFOR confirmed that one of its aircraft crashed during a routine operation and said no civilian infrastructure was damaged. Rescue teams were dispatched immediately.

Initial reporting by ANSA, citing Br?ko Mayor Siniša Mili?, put the toll at three dead and 12 injured. The supplied Dutch-language report subsequently quoted Br?ko hospital spokesperson Salih Ibrahimbegovi? as saying a fourth serviceman had died in hospital. The reports indicate that 15 people were aboard; their nationalities have not been confirmed.

The cause remains under investigation. EUFOR said it would conduct a full investigation and release further information once the facts had been established, urging the public to avoid circulating unverified claims.

据报道，2026 年 10 月 29 日，一架与 EUFOR Althea 一起执行任务的意大利陆军波音 CH-47 Chinook 在波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那布尔科区戈里察附近坠毁，造成 4 名军事人员死亡，另有 11 人受伤。
欧盟部队证实其一架飞机在例行行动中坠毁，并表示没有民用基础设施受损。救援队立即出动。
安莎社 (ANSA) 援引布尔科市长西尼萨·米利 (Siniša Mili?) 的消息称，此次事故造成 3 人死亡、12 人受伤。所提供的荷兰语报告随后引用了布尔科医院发言人萨利赫·易卜拉欣贝戈维 (Salih Ibrahimbegovi) 的话。据称第四名军人在医院死亡。报道称，机上共有 15 人；他们的国籍尚未得到确认。
原因仍在调查中。欧盟部队表示，一旦事实确定，将进行全面调查并发布进一步信息，并敦促公众避免传播未经证实的说法。

body_en: Air Montenegro to launch Brussels flights on 30 November alongside four new European routes - Aviation24.be

Air Montenegro will launch year-round flights between Podgorica and Brussels Airport on 30 November 2026, operating three return services per week. The connection is one of five routes scheduled under Montenegro’s one-year Public Service Obligation (PSO) programme, with tickets now on sale, according to the supplied reports.
Brussels flights will operate on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, with morning rotations from Podgorica on Mondays and Wednesdays and an afternoon rotation on Fridays.
All five routes will operate three times weekly throughout the year
Destination from Podgorica Launch date Zagreb 26 November 2026 Brussels Airport 30 November 2026 Frankfurt 4 December 2026 Paris Charles de Gaulle 17 December 2026 Bari 17 December 2026

Air Montenegro secured all five contracts as the sole bidder in a tender open to other airlines. Their combined estimated value is approximately €4.79 million excluding VAT, including €1.49 million earmarked for Brussels.

The Brussels allocation is not a guaranteed payment in full: compensation depends on actual revenue and eligible operating costs, with a permitted 5% profit margin and a contractual ceiling. The programme aims to improve Montenegro’s connectivity beyond the summer tourist season.

黑山航空将于 2026 年 11 月 30 日开通波德戈里察和布鲁塞尔机场之间的全年航班，每周运营 3 趟往返航班。据提供的报告称，这条航线是黑山一年期公共服务义务（PSO）计划中安排的五条航线之一，机票现已开始销售。
布鲁塞尔航班每周一、周三和周五运营，周一和周三上午轮换从波德戈里察起飞，周五下午轮换。
所有 5 条航线全年每周运营 3 趟

title_en: South African Airways Delaying Staff Pay, Yet Insists Finances Are Fine
title_zh: 南非航空公司推迟员工工资，但坚称财务状况良好
summary: South African Airways reportedly can't pay 30-40% of its staff, blaming fuel costs and prioritizing operations, while insisting it won't seek a bailout. The finances raise questions.
summary_zh: 据报道，南非航空公司无法支付 30-40% 员工的工资，原因是燃油成本和优先运营，同时坚称不会寻求白楼
body_en: South African Airways (SAA) has had pretty consistent financial issues for the past 15 or so years. In 2021, the airline emerged from “business rescue” with a clean balance sheet (and as a shell of its former self), and it has sort of been chugging along ever since.

However, the airline once again seems to be in a dire situation, as a large percentage of staff aren’t being paid. It’s anyone’s guess how this plays out, though executives at the company insist everything is fine.
South African Airways downplays financial issues

South African Airways is reportedly unable to pay 30-40% of its staff at the moment, claiming it has to prioritize critical operational costs. The airline is deferring salaries of management, pilots, executives, and board members, blaming the situation in rising fuel prices.

The company’s head of corporate affairs, Mpilo Dlamini, explained that SAA has struggled with insufficient capital injections since emerging from business rescue, though insists the airline won’t seek a bailout

“After the business rescue process, we did not get enough capital injection that is going to keep us afloat, cushion our costs, make sure that we expand the way we wanted to expand. So, there are those issues that I want to admit made us, you know, to be affected in terms of liquidity.”

“The board and the management are seized with making sure that we are actually the support that we got from government through the guarantee. We are talking and engaging a number of our financial institutions, and I must say and confirm to you now that they are willing and interested in supporting us because we have a bankable strategy. We are not going to ask for more money.”
There’s a lot of mystery surrounding the carrier’s finances

As flagged by View from the Wing , one certainly can’t help but be skeptical of all of the carrier’s financial claims. SAA’s annual financial report ending March 31, 2025, suggests that the airline group had a net profit of 155 million ZAR, or 9.3 million USD, while the airline as such had a net profit of 30 million ZAR, or 1.8 million USD.

Okay, that’s not exactly a huge profit, but at least it’s not a loss, right? Well, there’s more to the story. Before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization, the airline group had a loss of 317 million ZAR, or 19 million USD. And the airline also had gains of 1.169 billion ZAR, or 70.1 million USD, under the asset disposal line. This could partly be attributed to selling slots at Heathrow and a lease-modification gain.

The point is, it sounds like SAA wasn’t in a great financial situation before the current crisis, and also didn’t have much of a safety net. So the current situation is only making matters worse. While the company is downplaying how dire the situation is, typically you don’t have to pay pilots late if you’re in even a remotely decent situation. It’ll be interesting to see what’s next for the airline…

South African Airways is struggling to pay staff on-time, with up to 40% of employees having their pay deferred. The airline is blaming higher fuel prices, which are of course impacting the entire industry. South Africa’s national carrier has received billions in bailouts over the years, and claims everything is fine, but even the past numbers don’t exactly paint a great picture of the situation. South African’s “profit” over the last fully reported financial year was due to special items and the sale of slots, rather than an actual operating profit.
It sure seems like the airline may need a bailout sooner rather than later, or else it might be looking at some real issues, since you can’t just delay payment for staff on an ongoing basis.
What do you make of this South African Airways situation?
body_zh: 南非航空公司 (SAA) 在过去 15 年左右的时间里一直面临着相当严重的财务问题。 2021 年，该航空公司摆脱了“商业救援”，资产负债表干净（并且是以前的外壳），从那时起它就一直在稳步前进。
然而，该航空公司似乎再次陷入困境，因为很大一部分员工没有拿到工资。尽管公司高管坚称一切都很好，但谁也说不准事情会如何发展。
南非航空淡化财务问题
据报道，南非航空公司目前无法支付 30-40% 员工的工资，声称必须优先考虑关键的运营成本。该航空公司推迟了管理层、飞行员、高管和董事会成员的工资，并将原因归咎于燃油价格上涨。
该公司企业事务主管姆皮洛·德拉米尼 (Mpilo Dlamini) 解释说，南非航空自摆脱商业救助以来一直面临注资不足的问题，但坚称该航空公司不会寻求救助
“在企业救援过程之后，我们没有获得足够的资本注入来维持我们的生存，缓冲我们的成本，确保我们按照我们想要的方式扩张。因此，我想承认，有些问题使我们在流动性方面受到了影响。”
“董事会和管理层致力于确保我们实际上是通过担保从政府那里获得的支持。我们正在与我们的一些金融机构进行谈判和接触，我现在必须向你们确认，他们愿意并且有兴趣支持我们，因为我们有一个可融资的战略。我们不会要求更多的钱。”
该航空公司的财务状况存在很多谜团
正如《View from the Wing》所指出的那样，人们肯定会忍不住对这家航空公司的所有财务声明表示怀疑。 SAA截至2025年3月31日的年度财务报告显示，该航空集团的净利润为1.55亿南非兰特，即930万美元，而航空公司本身的净利润为3000万南非兰特，即180万美元。
好吧，这不完全是巨额利润，但至少不是亏损，对吧？嗯，这个故事还有更多内容。未计利息、税项、折旧及摊销前，该航空集团亏损 3.17 亿南非兰特，即 1900 万美元。该航空公司在资产处置额度下还获得了 11.69 亿南非兰特（约合 7010 万美元）的收益。这可能部分归因于希思罗机场航班时刻的出售和租赁修改收益。
关键是，听起来南非航空在当前危机之前的财务状况并不好，而且也没有太多的安全网。因此，目前的情况只会让事情变得更糟。虽然该公司淡化了情况的严重程度，但通常情况下，如果你的情况还算不错，你也不必迟付飞行员工资。看看该航空公司的下一步发展将会很有趣……
南非航空公司很难按时向员工支付工资，多达 40% 的员工被推迟支付工资。该航空公司将此归咎于燃油价格上涨，这当然影响了整个行业。南非国家航空公司多年来已获得数十亿美元的救助，并声称一切都很好，但即使是过去的数字也不能完全描绘出情况的美好图景。南非在上一个完整报告的财政年度的“利润”是由于特殊项目和老虎机的销售，而不是实际的营业利润。
看来航空公司可能需要尽快获得救助，否则它可能会考虑一些真正的问题，因为你不能只是持续推迟向员工支付工资。
您如何看待南非航空的这一情况？

title_en: Why The Airbus A321XLR Is Being Parked At JetBlue & Wizz Air, But Kept By Iberia & Qantas
title_zh: 为什么空客 A321XLR 停在捷蓝航空和威兹航空，却被伊比利亚航空和澳洲航空保留
summary: The A321XLR is working wonderfully for some airlines, but not for others. Here's what's causing these different operating experiences.
summary_zh: A321XLR 对于某些航空公司来说效果很好，但对于其他航空公司则不然。以下是导致这些不同操作体验的原因。
body_en: Why The Airbus A321XLR Is Being Parked At JetBlue & Wizz Air, But Kept By Iberia & Qantas

Daniel comes to Simple Flying with a business focused approach to the aviation world. Daniel enjoys analyzing strategy and how companies move against each other to gain a step ahead in the skies. Besides strategy, Daniel also has a passion for aircraft design and the history of aviation.

The Airbus A321XLR was one of the most highly anticipated aircraft types to come out in recent years, given its small size, low operating costs, and excellent range. Airbus had already made a long-range narrowbody with the A321LR, but the A321XLR is essentially an improved version of the same aircraft, with even more range than the famed Boeing 757. It's been in service for almost two years now, and the type's operations during this time, as well as its general market reception, have been interesting.

Iberia and Qantas have been positive about the plane. Wizz Air, on the other hand, has canceled most of its A321XLR orders and is parking the examples that have already arrived. JetBlue, which planned to operate the A321XLR transatlantic in a premium-heavy layout, has deferred most of its order and sold its first two production slots to Aegean Airlines, which then canceled the orders. Meanwhile, Air Canada and United Airlines have expressed concerns about its performance and capabilities.

Iberia, which is owned by IAG, was the launch operator for the A321XLR, flying its first commercial service on November 6, 2024 . Aer Lingus, also an IAG carrier, soon followed, and the A321XLR is now also operated by Air Canada, American Airlines, IndiGo, Qanot Sharq, Qantas, Saudia, United Airlines, and Wizz Air, as per Cirium . So far, Iberia has praised the A321XLR, stating that the type burns up to 40% less fuel than widebody models , and it's also operating what was, until recently, the world's longest A321XLR flight from Madrid to Santo Domingo.

A380 747 787 A350 777 737 MAX A320neo More types

Iberia, like most A321XLR customers, configured the type with lie-flat seats to operate long-distance flights, but Qantas has not. Instead, the Australian flag carrier installs 197-200 seats (depending on the layout), recliner seats, and uses the aircraft mainly for domestic flights. For Qantas, it's the payload that's appealing rather than just the range, although it will also operate longer routes with the A321XLR. As it stands, Qantas will be expanding the type's use, including using it on international flights and creating a subfleet with lie-flats.

Aer Lingus has positively commented on the A321XLR, while Qantas has publicly commented that customer reception to the aircraft has been excellent. The plane is proving to be fuel-efficient, with Iberia stating that it burns less fuel than expected. Iberia and Aer Lingus have deployed the A321XLR extensively throughout their networks, while Qantas plans to use the aircraft in a variety of roles. Meanwhile, IndiGo has recently begun operating the world's longest A321XLR flight, from Mumbai to Amsterdam.

Wizz Air and JetBlue's experience with the A321XLR seems to contradict the positive experiences being reported by IAG and Qantas. Wizz Air converted 36 A321XLR orders to the standard A321neo model, leaving it with just 11 examples total , and five of the planes it's already taken are currently stored. Meanwhile, JetBlue deferred 11 of its 13 A321XLRs, while the first two were sold to Aegean, then were subsequently rejected. However, there were unique circumstances surrounding each of these events.

Wizz Air mainly acquired 47 A321XLRs for its Abu Dhabi subsidiary, but it ended up shutting down the Abu Dhabi operations in September 2025. With these, the carrier had no use for most of these planes, since a long-range narrowbody generally doesn't fit with its business model of operating all-economy budget flights within Europe. The airline is operating these planes well below their range limit, while it's stored five examples to strip them of their engines due to the current shortage of Pratt & Whitney GTF engines.

The deferment of the A321XLRs came as part of a larger deferment in which 44 A321neos (including the XLRs) were pushed back to 2030 and beyond. The delivery dates for the airline's first two XLRs were too close to be deferred, and JetBlue therefore sold them to avoid operating a two-aircraft orphan fleet for five years . Aegean acquired the planes to gain short-term capacity, but seat delivery delays meant that they wouldn't be ready until after the lucrative summer season, and the airline rejected them to avoid an orphan fleet.

United Airlines ordered 50 A321XLRs to replace its Boeing 757-200 fleet and expand its network of thin long-haul routes. However, the carrier has expressed disappointment with the plane's true range, stating that it cannot reliably operate routes such as from Newark to Italy despite being marketed with this capability. Meanwhile, Air Canada has expressed concern about how the plane's range and payload are impacted by hot weather conditions and challenging airfields.

The A321XLR has gained weight compared to its original promises, due to extra fire protection in the plane's Rear Centre Tank (RCT) mandated by regulators. Airbus has bumped the plane's Maximum Takeoff Weight (MTOW) to 101.5 tons to offset this, but it's still heavy for its size, especially considering how heavy modern lie-flat business class seats are. In addition, the aircraft's brochure range of 4,700 NM (8,700 km) is calculated using favorable wind conditions, a light configuration, and an optional auxiliary center tank (ACT).

Brochure ranges for every aircraft are calculated using favorable conditions, and any plane will be impacted by challenging field conditions. However, the A321XLR's range is good for a narrowbody, but it can prove restrictive for airlines looking to operate longer transatlantic services, whereas modern widebodies have substantially more 'margin'. Essentially all modern long-haul planes also have heavy lie-flat seats, but the A321XLR is more heavily impacted by these because it's smaller and lighter overall.

In United's case specifically, the airline did not option the forward ACT, which may explain why United could struggle with some of the routes it had planned. In comparison, American Airlines is reported to have selected the ACT, allowing it to plan routes like Philadelphia-Vienna that are longer than Newark-Italy. With Air Canada, meanwhile, the A321XLR operates close to its maximum capabilities more often than widebodies, which means that flights are more heavily impacted by challenging airfields.
body_zh: 为什么空客 A321XLR 停在捷蓝航空和威兹航空，却被伊比利亚航空和澳洲航空保留
Daniel 带着以商业为中心的方式进入航空界，加入了 Simple Flying。丹尼尔喜欢分析战略以及公司如何相互竞争以取得领先一步。除了战略之外，丹尼尔还对飞机设计和航空历史充满热情。
空客 A321XLR 因其体积小、运营成本低和航程出色而成为近年来最受期待的飞机类型之一。空中客车公司已经用 A321LR 制造了远程窄体飞机，但 A321XLR 本质上是同一架飞机的改进版本，其航程甚至比著名的波音 757 还要大。它已经服役近两年了，该机型在此期间的运营情况以及总体市场反响都很有趣。
伊比利亚航空和澳洲航空对这架飞机持积极态度。另一方面，威兹航空 (Wizz Air) 取消了大部分 A321XLR 订单，并停放了已抵达的订单。捷蓝航空原本计划以高端重型布局运营 A321XLR 跨大西洋航线，但已推迟了大部分订单，并将其前两个生产舱位出售给爱琴海航空，爱琴海航空随后取消了订单。与此同时，加拿大航空和联合航空对其表现和能力表示担忧。

IAG 旗下的伊比利亚航空是 A321XLR 的发射运营商，于 2024 年 11 月 6 日首次进行商业服务。根据 Cirium 的说法，同样是 IAG 航空公司的爱尔兰航空 (Aer Lingus) 也紧随其后，现在加拿大航空、美国航空、靛蓝航空、Qanot Sharq、澳洲航空、沙特阿拉伯航空、联合航空和维兹航空也运营 A321XLR。到目前为止，伊比利亚航空对 A321XLR 表示赞扬，称该机型比宽体机型节省了 40% 的燃油，而且直到最近，该公司还在运营从马德里飞往圣多明各的世界上最长的 A321XLR 航班。
选择一架飞机，看看现在有多少架飞机在空中

与大多数 A321XLR 客户一样，伊比利亚航空为该机型配置了平躺式座椅以运营长途航班，但澳洲航空却没有。相反，这家澳大利亚旗舰航空公司安装了 197-200 个座位（取决于布局）、躺椅，并将飞机主要用于国内航班。对于澳洲航空来说，吸引人的是有效载荷而不仅仅是航程，尽管它也将使用 A321XLR 运营更长的航线。目前，澳洲航空将扩大该机型的使用范围，包括在国际航班上使用该机型，并创建一支配备平躺式飞机的子机队。
爱尔兰航空对 A321XLR 给予积极评价，而澳洲航空则公开表示客户对这架飞机的接待非常好。事实证明，这架飞机具有燃油效率，伊比利亚航空表示，它燃烧的燃油比预期要少。伊比利亚航空和爱尔兰航空已在其网络中广泛部署了 A321XLR，而澳洲航空则计划将该飞机用于多种用途。与此同时，靛蓝航空最近开始运营世界上最长的 A321XLR 航班，从孟买飞往阿姆斯特丹。
威兹航空和捷蓝航空在 A321XLR 上的体验似乎与 IAG 和澳洲航空报道的积极体验相矛盾。 Wizz Air 将 36 架 A321XLR 订单转换为标准 A321neo 型号，总共只剩下 11 架，其中 5 架已订购的飞机目前已被存储。与此同时，捷蓝航空推迟了其 13 架 A321XLR 中的 11 架，而前两架被出售给爱琴海，但随后被拒绝。然而，每个事件都有独特的情况。
威兹航空主要为其阿布扎比子公司采购了 47 架 A321XLR，但最终于 2025 年 9 月关闭了阿布扎比业务。因此，该航空公司不再使用其中的大部分飞机，因为远程窄体飞机通常不适合其在欧洲境内运营全经济型廉价航班的商业模式。该航空公司正在以远低于航程限制的速度运营这些飞机，同时由于目前普拉特惠特尼 GTF 发动机短缺，该航空公司还储存了五架飞机以拆除发动机。

A321XLR 的推迟是更大规模推迟的一部分，其中 44 架 A321neo（包括 XLR）被推迟到 2030 年及以后。该航空公司前两架 XLR 飞机的交付日期太接近，无法推迟，因此捷蓝航空出售了它们，以避免在五年内运营两架飞机的孤儿机队。爱琴海航空公司购买这些飞机是为了获得短期运力，但座位交付延误意味着这些飞机要到利润丰厚的夏季过后才能准备就绪，因此该航空公司拒绝了这些飞机，以避免出现孤儿机队。
美国联合航空公司订购了 50 架 A321XLR 来替换其波音 757-200 机队并扩大其稀疏的长途航线网络。然而，该航空公司对该飞机的真实航程表示失望，称尽管在营销时具有这种能力，但它无法可靠地运营从纽瓦克到意大利等航线。与此同时，加拿大航空对炎热天气条件和充满挑战的机场对飞机航程和有效载荷的影响表示担忧。

由于监管机构要求在飞机后中心油箱 (RCT) 中提供额外的防火保护，A321XLR 与最初承诺的重量相比有所增加。空中客车公司已将飞机的最大起飞重量 (MTOW) 提高至 101.5 吨，以抵消这一影响，但就其尺寸而言，它仍然很重，特别是考虑到现代平躺式商务舱座椅的重量。此外，该飞机的宣传航程为 4,700 海里（8,700 公里），是根据有利的风力条件、轻型配置和可选的辅助中心油箱 (ACT) 计算得出的。
每架飞机的手册航程都是根据有利条件计算的，任何飞机都会受到挑战性现场条件的影响。然而，A321XLR 的航程对于窄体机来说是有利的，但对于希望运营更长的跨大西洋航班的航空公司来说可能会受到限制，而现代宽体机则拥有更多的“利润”。基本上所有现代长途飞机都配备了重型平躺式座椅，但 A321XLR 受这些影响更严重，因为它整体更小、更轻。
具体以美联航为例，该航空公司没有选择转发 ACT，这也许可以解释为什么美联航可能会在其计划的某些航线上遇到困难。相比之下，据报道美国航空选择了ACT，使其可以规划费城-维也纳等比纽瓦克-意大利更长的航线。与此同时，加拿大航空的 A321XLR 比宽体机更频繁地接近其最大能力，这意味着航班更容易受到具有挑战性的机场的影响。

title_en: United CEO Scott Kirby Insists Critics Misunderstand His American Merger Vision
title_zh: 美联航首席执行官斯科特·柯比坚称批评者误解了他的美国合并愿景
summary: In a new interview, United CEO Scott Kirby says critics misunderstand his proposed merger with American, and that he alone knows the plan. Here's why I disagree.
summary_zh: 在一次新的采访中，美联航首席执行官斯科特·柯比表示，批评者误解了他与美国航空合并的提议，只有他自己知道这个计划。这就是为什么
body_en: In April 2026, news broke about how United CEO Scott Kirby reportedly approached the Trump administration about the concept of merging with American, and forming a “flag” carrier for the United States.

Days later, American management publicly rejected this concept , which caused Kirby to publicly make his case for a merger with American . Months later, it came out that Kirby had also approached Delta about the concept of a merger . There’s now an interesting update on this — Kirby is still hell-bent on this concept, and thinks everyone else is wrong.
Kirby insists people don’t understand his merger vision

The Dallas Morning News has a fascinating interview with Kirby. For those curious about the connection here, keep in mind that Kirby lives in Dallas (he never moved, since being fired from American over a decade ago). Kirby does so many interviews that you’d think he has a movie dropping in theaters soon, and he always has a lot of interesting takes on things.
What’s most interesting to me about this interview is how Kirby talks more about the merger concept he had with American. According to Kirby’s version of events
News of this became public when Trump administration officials (or someone with knowledge of the matter) leaked details about how Kirby had approached them
Kirby claims he had engaged in conversations with American management, and while they were “skeptical,” “they talked to us and they hadn’t said no”

American then released a public statement rejecting the concept of a merger — Kirby had reportedly been texting with American CEO Robert Isom, and Kirby told Isom that he saw the public statement rejecting the idea, and was surprised by that
But here’s the most interesting part of Kirby’s statement

“We were disappointed that it leaked and then I saw all of the feedback of what people said about how possible it was. All of the criticism about this would not get through regulatory muscle was looking at it through a traditional commodity lens, and I am the one person who knows what we were planning to do for 100% certainty because I’m the one that was going to do it.”

So in April 2026, following American’s public denial of the merger, Kirby was at luxury resort Amangiri in Utah. While his wife was at the spa, he began writing a message about why he thought a merger made sense, which ended up being published online.
Kirby’s conviction was seemingly strengthened by what parents would tell him at his kid’s soccer game

“You know I live in Dallas, for the first month [after the message was released] every time I was at my kid’s soccer game, some stranger would come up to me and say is it really dead, can you please buy [American]. It actually made me even more firm in my belief that there’s a hunger [from] customers for great customer service. That deal would have been a home run for customers.”
Kirby’s steadfastness is admirable, or something

I have a ton of respect for what Kirby has done at United, and how he has transformed the airline, though he’s also a puzzling guy, in terms of what he shares with the public. Keep in mind that before he got into the airline industry, Kirby was big into gambling . When Kirby makes certain statements in an interview, one can’t help but wonder if he just can’t hold back and is being honest, or if he’s largely bluffing.

I do believe Kirby cares a lot about (broadly) offering a quality product, and I can concede that if American and United merged, I do think the quality of the overall product would be better. Well, or at least that would be the case in comparison to American today, though we know the airline is also working on improving, and is trying to become more like United.

Here’s the fundamental disagreement I have with Kirby, though. I know both Delta and United like to think of themselves as these cool lifestyle brands that consumers really like. I can also appreciate the concept of trying to create brand loyal customers and the attempted decommodification of the industry.

But that fails to consider that while some percentage of customers are loyal and love an airline, a majority of people are still just looking to get between two points with the best overall value, which we’d define as a combination of the best schedule, price, and product.

If you create one US flag carrier that has around 40% of the market share in the country, that would without a doubt lead to higher fares in the long run. And that’s not even something Kirby seems to disagree with, conceptually. He has long argued that airfare has become too cheap in recent times, and that the fare increases we’re seeing due to higher oil prices will stick around even when oil prices go down .

Kirby points out how most airlines aren’t profitable, so fares will need to go up for that to change (while of course discounting the billions in profits that airlines make through their loyalty programs).
body_zh: 2026 年 4 月，有消息称美联航首席执行官斯科特·柯比 (Scott Kirby) 就与美国航空合并并组建美国“旗舰”航空公司的概念与特朗普政府接洽。
几天后，美国航空公司管理层公开拒绝了这一概念，这导致柯比公开提出与美国航空公司合并的理由。几个月后，有消息称，柯比也曾与达美航空就合并的概念进行过接触。现在有一个有趣的更新——柯比仍然执着于这个概念，并认为其他人都是错的。
柯比坚称人们不理解他的合并愿景
《达拉斯晨报》对柯比进行了精彩的采访。对于那些对这里的联系感到好奇的人，请记住柯比住在达拉斯（自从十多年前被美国航空解雇以来，他从未搬过家）。柯比接受了如此多的采访，以至于你会认为他的电影很快就会在影院上映，而且他总是对事物有很多有趣的看法。
这次采访中最让我感兴趣的是柯比如何更多地谈论他与美国航空公司的合并概念。根据卡比的事件版本
当特朗普政府官员（或知情人士）泄露了柯比如何接触他们的细节时，这一消息就被公开了
柯比声称他已经与美国管理层进行了对话，虽然他们“持怀疑态度”，但“他们与我们交谈，但他们没有拒绝”
美国航空随后发布了一份公开声明，拒绝合并的概念——据报道，柯比一直在与美国航空首席执行官罗伯特·伊索姆发短信，柯比告诉伊索姆，他看到了拒绝这一想法的公开声明，对此感到惊讶
但这是柯比声明中最有趣的部分
“我们对它的泄露感到失望，然后我看到了人们所说的关于它的可能性的所有反馈。所有关于这件事的批评都不会通过监管机构，而是通过传统的商品镜头来看待它，而我是一个百分百确定地知道我们计划做什么的人，因为我就是那个要做这件事的人。”
因此，2026 年 4 月，在美国航空公开否认合并之后，柯比来到了犹他州的豪华度假村阿曼吉里。当他的妻子在水疗中心时，他开始写一条信息，解释为什么他认为合并是有意义的，该信息最终发布在网上。
父母在孩子的足球比赛中告诉他的话似乎更加坚定了柯比的信念
“你知道我住在达拉斯，[消息发布后]的第一个月，每次我看孩子的足球比赛时，都会有陌生人过来对我说，它真的死了吗？你能买[美国]吗？这实际上让我更加坚定了我的信念，即客户渴望优质的客户服务。这笔交易对客户来说将是一次全垒打。”
卡比的坚定令人钦佩，或者什么
我非常尊重柯比在美联航所做的一切，以及他如何改变了这家航空公司，尽管就他与公众分享的内容而言，他也是一个令人费解的人。请记住，在进入航空业之前，柯比热衷于赌博。当柯比在接受采访时发表某些言论时，人们不禁想知道他是否无法克制并诚实，或者他是否在很大程度上虚张声势。
我确实相信柯比非常关心（广泛地）提供优质产品，而且我可以承认，如果美国航空和联合航空合并，我确实认为整体产品的质量会更好。嗯，或者至少与今天的美国航空相比是这样，尽管我们知道该航空公司也在努力改进，并试图变得更像联合航空。
不过，这是我与柯比的根本分歧。我知道达美航空和美联航都喜欢将自己视为消费者真正喜欢的炫酷生活方式品牌。我还可以欣赏尝试创建品牌忠诚客户的概念以及尝试对行业进行去商品化的尝试。
但这没有考虑到，虽然有一定比例的客户是忠诚的并且喜欢一家航空公司，但大多数人仍然只是寻求在两点之间获得最佳整体价值，我们将其定义为最佳时刻表、价格和产品的组合。
如果你创建一家拥有该国约 40% 市场份额的美国旗舰航空公司，从长远来看，毫无疑问会导致票价上涨。从概念上讲，柯比似乎也不反对这一点。他长期以来一直认为，近年来机票变得太便宜了，而且即使油价下跌，我们所看到的由于油价上涨而导致的票价上涨也会持续存在。
柯比指出，大多数航空公司都无法盈利，因此需要提高票价才能改变这种情况（当然，这要扣除航空公司通过忠诚度计划赚取的数十亿利润）。

title_en: Why Premium Economy Is Effectively Yesterday's Standard Economy: Pitch Shrank From 34 Inches To 30-31
title_zh: 为什么豪华经济舱实际上是昨天的标准经济舱：节距从 34 英寸缩小到 30-31 英寸
summary: Economy class has seen some stark changes over the years.
summary_zh: 多年来，经济舱发生了一些明显的变化。
body_en: Why Premium Economy Is Effectively Yesterday's Standard Economy: Pitch Shrank From 34 Inches To 30-31

Journalist - Steven has a varied background in communications, and it was this passion for writing combined with his in-depth knowledge of the aviation industry that led him to Simple Flying. A keen linguist, he also has experience in translation and interpreting. Based in Palma, Spain

For years, a standard economy class seat with 34 inches of pitch represented a reasonably comfortable way to fly long-haul, giving passengers enough room to stretch their legs without paying the substantial premium associated with business class. Today, however, that kind of space is increasingly difficult to find across standard economy class cabins, where 30 or 31 inches has become the norm for long-haul services.

As such, the additional room that once helped define conventional seating is now frequently marketed as a premium product . The transformation is not simply a story about airlines squeezing more passengers into aircraft, although cabin density remains important. Instead, it reflects a broader shift in airline economics.

Specifically, revenue per square foot increasingly determines how cabins are designed and how comfort is priced. Premium economy has consequently evolved from a niche upgrade into something resembling yesterday's standard economy class, while basic economy at the opposite end of the pricing spectrum has helped create an increasingly polarized onboard experience.

Seat pitch measures the distance between corresponding points on two seats in successive rows, rather than the unobstructed space available to a passenger's knees, but it remains one of the most useful indicators of how an airline allocates cabin space. A 34-inch seat pitch was once associated with relatively generous economy class seating, particularly on longer international routes.

Meanwhile, contemporary configurations commonly place passengers approximately 30 to 32 inches apart, depending on the airline, aircraft, and route. The difference between 34 and 30 inches might appear insignificant numerically, yet losing four inches can materially affect the experience of sitting upright for hours, particularly for taller passengers whose knees already approach the seat ahead.

A 31-inch configuration represents a smaller reduction, but the cumulative effect becomes noticeable when passengers cannot stretch comfortably, change position easily, or find a relaxed posture during an overnight journey. Aircraft type also matters because cabin width, seat design, and the number of seats installed across each row influence the overall experience .

With the majority of carriers, including the likes of American Airlines and United Airlines , the Boeing 787 Dreamliner features a 3-3-3 layout in economy class, while the Boeing 777 can accommodate an extra seat in a 3-4-3 layout. There is also a distinction between the space an airline provides and the space it advertises.

This is because identical pitch measurements can produce different experiences depending on seat thickness, recline mechanisms, and cushion design. Nevertheless, the broader trend is clear: passengers increasingly encounter less room in standard economy while paying separately for the additional space that once helped define a conventional seat.

The explanation lies in aircraft interior economics, where every additional inch of cabin space carries an opportunity cost because it could accommodate another passenger or contribute to a higher-value seating arrangement. Airlines balance operating expenses, aircraft utilization, passenger demand, and ticket revenue, and even small changes to a cabin layout can influence how much money an aircraft generates on each departure.

Business class illustrates the incentive particularly clearly, since a premium seat can occupy two to four times the space of an economy class seat while commanding a substantially higher fare. Industry estimates suggest business class can generate four to five times as much revenue per square foot as economy class, while premium economy can deliver approximately 1.8 to 2.4 times economy's revenue for around 1.5 times the footprint.

These estimates vary by route, aircraft , and demand, but they explain why airlines increasingly prioritize cabin mix rather than passenger numbers alone. Selling fewer seats at significantly higher prices can sometimes generate better returns than maximizing capacity, particularly on routes where corporate travelers and affluent leisure passengers demonstrate strong willingness to pay for additional comfort.

The result is a commercial calculation favoring high-yield premium seating alongside a densely configured economy class cabin, creating what is often described as a barbell-shaped aircraft interior. Business class attracts passengers paying for privacy and luxury, while economy class retains travelers seeking competitive fares, leaving premium economy to capture those willing to spend more without paying for a lie-flat seat.

Premium economy was originally positioned as an intermediate option for travelers who wanted something better than standard economy but could not justify business-class prices. Its appeal rested on wider seats, additional legroom, greater recline, and selected service enhancements, allowing airlines to sell a meaningful upgrade without dedicating as much cabin space to each passenger as business class requires.

As carriers refined their offerings, however, premium economy increasingly became a distinct revenue category rather than simply a small collection of especially comfortable seats toward the front of economy. On long-haul aircraft, such as the Airbus A350 , the cabin can offer a quieter environment, improved dining and other benefits alongside its physical advantages, although the exact package differs between airlines.

The irony is that some of the room passengers now pay extra to obtain resembles the space available in older economy configurations. Premium economy seats frequently provide pitches in the mid-to-upper 30-inch range, although individual products vary, bringing them closer to traditional expectations of standard seating than the increasingly common 30- or 31-inch economy arrangement.

For airlines, this creates an opportunity to monetize comfort without making every ticket more expensive. Passengers prioritizing legroom can purchase an upgrade, while price-sensitive travelers remain in economy class or select basic economy. The commercial strategy captures different willingness to pay, but it also means that comfort once associated with an ordinary ticket increasingly depends on selecting the correct fare category.
body_zh: 为什么豪华经济舱实际上是昨天的标准经济舱：节距从 34 英寸缩小到 30-31 英寸
记者 - 史蒂文在传播领域拥有不同的背景，正是这种对写作的热情与他对航空业的深入了解相结合，促使他创立了《简单飞行》。作为一位敏锐的语言学家，他还拥有翻译和口译经验。总部位于西班牙帕尔马
多年来，34 英寸间距的标准经济舱座椅代表了一种相当舒适的长途飞行方式，为乘客提供了足够的空间来伸展双腿，而无需支付与商务舱相关的高额费用。然而如今，在标准经济舱中越来越难找到这样的空间，30 或 31 英寸已成为长途服务的标准。
因此，曾经帮助定义传统座椅的额外空间现在经常作为优质产品进行销售。尽管客舱密度仍然很重要，但这种转变不仅仅是航空公司将更多乘客挤进飞机的故事。相反，它反映了航空经济的更广泛转变。
具体来说，每平方英尺的收入越来越多地决定了客舱的设计方式以及舒适度的定价方式。因此，高端经济舱已经从利基升级演变成类似昨天的标准经济舱的东西，而定价范围另一端的基础经济舱则帮助创造了日益两极分化的机上体验。
座椅间距测量的是连续排中两个座椅上对应点之间的距离，而不是乘客膝盖可用的无障碍空间，但它仍然是航空公司如何分配机舱空间的最有用的指标之一。 34 英寸的座椅间距曾经与相对宽敞的经济舱座位联系在一起，尤其是在长途国际航线上。
与此同时，现代配置通常使乘客之间的距离约为 30 至 32 英寸，具体取决于航空公司、飞机和航线。 34 英寸和 30 英寸之间的差异在数字上可能显得微不足道，但减少 4 英寸可能会严重影响直立坐几个小时的体验，特别是对于膝盖已经接近前方座位的较高乘客而言。
31 英寸的配置代表较小的减少，但当乘客在夜间旅行中无法舒适地伸展、轻松改变位置或找到放松的姿势时，累积效应就会变得明显。飞机类型也很重要，因为机舱宽度、座椅设计以及每排安装的座椅数量都会影响整体体验。
大多数航空公司，包括美国航空和联合航空等，波音 787 梦想飞机的经济舱采用 3-3-3 布局，而波音 777 则可在 3-4-3 布局中容纳一个额外的座位。航空公司提供的舱位与其广告中的舱位之间也存在区别。
这是因为，根据座椅厚度、倾斜机制和座垫设计，相同的间距测量可能会产生不同的体验。尽管如此，更广泛的趋势是明确的：乘客在标准经济舱中遇到的空间越来越少，同时为曾经有助于定义传统座位的额外空间单独付费。
解释在于飞机内部经济学，每增加一英寸的机舱空间都会带来机会成本，因为它可以容纳另一名乘客或有助于更高价值的座位安排。航空公司平衡运营费用、飞机利用率、乘客需求和机票收入，甚至客舱布局的微小变化也会影响飞机每次起飞的收入。
商务舱尤其清楚地说明了这一激励措施，因为高级座位所占用的空间是经济舱座位的两到四倍，而票价却要高得多。行业估计表明，商务舱每平方英尺产生的收入是经济舱的四到五倍，而豪华经济舱可以在约 1.5 倍的占地面积内提供约 1.8 到 2.4 倍的经济收入。
这些估计因航线、飞机和需求而异，但它们解释了为什么航空公司越来越重视客舱组合，而不仅仅是乘客数量。以高得多的价格出售更少的座位有时比最大化运力能产生更好的回报，特别是在商务旅客和富裕休闲旅客表现出强烈愿意为额外舒适度付费的航线上。
其结果是商业计算倾向于在密集配置的经济舱旁边配备高产量的高级座椅，从而创造出通常被描述为杠铃形的飞机内部空间。商务舱吸引了为隐私和奢华付费的乘客，而经济舱则留住了寻求有竞争力票价的乘客，而高端经济舱则吸引了那些愿意花更多钱而不支付平躺座位费用的乘客。
高级经济舱最初被定位为想要比标准经济舱更好但无法证明商务舱价格合理的旅行者的中间选择。它的吸引力在于更宽的座位、更多的腿部空间、更大的倾斜度和选择性的服务增强，使航空公司能够出售有意义的升级，而无需为每位乘客提供商务舱所需的那么多机舱空间。
然而，随着航空公司完善其产品，豪华经济舱日益成为一个独特的收入类别，而不仅仅是经济舱前部的一小部分特别舒适的座位。在空客 A350 等长途飞机上，客舱除了物理优势之外，还可以提供更安静的环境、更好的餐饮和其他好处，尽管具体的套餐因航空公司而异。
具有讽刺意味的是，一些房间的乘客现在支付额外费用才能获得类似于旧经济舱配置中的可用空间。高级经济舱座椅通常提供中上 30 英寸范围内的间距，尽管个别产品有所不同，但与日益常见的 30 或 31 英寸经济舱布局相比，它们更接近标准座椅的传统预期。
对于航空公司来说，这创造了一个通过舒适度货币化的机会，而不会让每张机票变得更加昂贵。优先考虑腿部空间的乘客可以购买升舱，而对价格敏感的乘客则继续乘坐经济舱或选择基础经济舱。商业策略抓住了不同的支付意愿，但这也意味着曾经与普通机票相关的舒适度越来越依赖于选择正确的票价类别。

title_en: Alaska Airlines Is Betting On Seatback Screens For Only A Fraction Of Seats On Its Transcon Boeing 737 MAX 10s
title_zh: 阿拉斯加航空押注于其 Transcon 波音 737 MAX 10 飞机上仅一小部分座位的座椅靠背屏幕
summary: The newest single-aisle joining Alaska's fleet is comes with a BYOD cabin policy.
summary_zh: 阿拉斯加机队最新的单通道飞机配备了 BYOD 客舱政策。
body_en: Alaska Airlines Is Betting On Seatback Screens For Only A Fraction Of Seats On Its Transcon Boeing 737 MAX 10s

Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

Anticipating the debut of its first Boeing 737 MAX 10 , Alaska Airlines has announced its new in-flight entertainment (IFE) design, which will starkly divide the experience in the front of the cabin from the back of the jet. Only the two most expensive cabins get screens, which works out to roughly 15% of about 159 seats. Passengers in every other row will be on a bring-your-own-device plan (BYOD).

Splitting a cabin this way is rare. PaxEx commented that Copa Airlines may be the only other carrier doing something similar, which makes the choice stand out. Alaska announced the layout on September 29, at its Investor Day in Seattle. The new jet will be equipped with lie-flat Aurora Suites to fly on select transcontinental routes from 2028.

Alaska has historically been opposed to seatback IFE for its single-aisle fleet to cut down on airplane weight. The Boeing 737 MAX 10 has already faced years of severe certification delays. Alaska also noted that keeping screens out of the main cabin helps them avoid further complex hardware certification delays so they can get the planes in the air faster. The airline is counting on free Starlink WiFi being enough to satisfy customers and make seatback screens unnecessary.

The Alaska plan for the MAX 10 includes four cabins . Aurora Suites will be at the front, followed by its new, and first true premium economy class: Premium Reserve. Behind that will come Premium Class, which is actually just extra-legroom economy. Finally, there will be a Main Cabin with standard economy seating. According to Live And Let's Fly, only the first two cabins get seatback screens on Panasonic's Astrova system . Premium Class and Main Cabin passengers will use their own devices.

The table below breaks down the key differences between the different cabin classes on the upcoming MAX 10. The appearance of the Aurora Suites on the 737 airframe will also be a first for the airline. Notably, not every plane in the upcoming delivery of the 105 MAX 10s will be equipped with the same layout. Alaska has said that at least 25 will be configured using this arrangement.

Alaska executives framed the premium experience as being about the suites and Premium Reserve, while Main Cabin would resemble the rest of the fleet, according to APEX. Alaska's Boeing narrowbodies have never offered built-in entertainment, and the Airbus jets inherited from Virgin America lost theirs after the merger. The airline expects its first MAX 10 delivery in the second quarter of 2027, but the lie-flat seats will not be installed until 2028.

The Federal Aviation Administration officially certified the Boeing 737 MAX 10, clearing the final hurdle after years of delays on October 20. Now, Alaska expects to take delivery of 22 MAX 10 aircraft throughout 2027. To get these planes into service as quickly as possible and avoid any further delays, this initial batch will feature Alaska's standard, high-density domestic cabin layout with 188 seats.

Like the rest of Alaska's current fleet, these 2027 planes will be strictly BYOD across all rows. The 25 aircraft equipped with the Aurora Suite will be a special premium heavy subfleet. This is the specific 2028 fleet that will introduce the 19-inch (48.26 cm) and 16-inch (40.64 cm) 4K screens to the front of the plane while keeping the back of the aircraft bare. The delay was unplanned, as Alaska did not know that the seats were still pending FAA approval when it unveiled the design to the public.

The primary reason for the delay is that the FAA subjects lie-flat premium seats to intense 16G dynamic crash testing. Traditional seats face straight forward, which makes managing crash impact forces relatively predictable. Lie-flat suites on single-aisle jets are typically installed at an angle. The FAA requires extensive sled-testing to prove that a human body positioned at an angle can survive a 16-G-force impact without hitting the suite walls or suffering severe neck and spinal trauma.

To pass the FAA's strict head-injury criteria during a crash, angled lie-flat suites will require highly complex, inflatable airbag seatbelts. The FAA must also certify the entire cabin installation as a single system. Then the FAA must inspect to confirm the structures do not block emergency egress paths for the rest of the plane. Designing, testing, and adjusting the shell materials to pass these specific impact regulations routinely takes seat manufacturers 18 to 24 months.

The successful rollout of Starlink on the Hawaiian Airlines Airbus A330 fleet served as the proof-of-concept for Alaska. The pilot program launched on Honolulu's widebodies directly informed the corporate leaders and gave Alaska Air Group the confidence to cut seatback screens from the main cabin of the upcoming 737 MAX 10.

However, Beat of Hawaii questioned how much that data proves . Hawaiian's older screens were dated, which makes declining use harder to read as a verdict on seatback entertainment itself. A passenger who ignores an aging display has not necessarily rejected screens. The data may simply be related to a problem with Hawaiian's hardware rather than seatback IFE overall.

These widebodies fly some of the most isolated routes in the world across the Pacific Ocean, entirely dependent on satellite coverage. Operational data proved that Starlink delivered gate-to-gate, low-latency broadband. The successful introduction of a route that passes over a vast span of remote Oceanic airspace also shows that the same coverage should be reliable over the continental US.

Hawaii essentially acted as the guinea pig. When given access to free, ground-speed internet, a massive percentage of travelers actively bypass the airline's built-in entertainment system. The A330 data also highlighted where built-in screens still matter: the premium market. Passengers paying top-tier fares expect an all-inclusive, luxury environment where they do not have to prop up a phone.

Alaska heavily values an identical narrowbody cabin in their fleet so they can swap aircraft seamlessly if a flight is delayed or canceled. Because their current 737-800s, 737-900ERs, and MAX 9s are completely screenless, introducing screens to the back of only the MAX 10 would create a highly inconsistent passenger experience if an aircraft swap occurred. Still, there are some caveats to this overarching strategy.
body_zh: 阿拉斯加航空押注于其 Transcon 波音 737 MAX 10 飞机上仅一小部分座位的座椅靠背屏幕
卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
预计首架波音 737 MAX 10 即将首次亮相，阿拉斯加航空宣布了其全新的机上娱乐 (IFE) 设计，该设计将把机舱前部的体验与飞机后部的体验截然不同。只有两个最昂贵的客舱配有屏幕，约占 159 个座位的 15%。每隔一排的乘客都将采用自带设备计划 (BYOD)。
以这种方式分割小屋的情况很少见。 PaxEx 评论说，巴拿马航空可能是唯一一家做类似事情的其他航空公司，这使得选择脱颖而出。阿拉斯加于 9 月 29 日在西雅图举行的投资者日宣布了这一布局。这架新型喷气式飞机将配备平躺式 Aurora 套房，从 2028 年起将在部分洲际航线上飞行。
阿拉斯加航空公司历来反对为其单通道机队采用座椅靠背机载娱乐系统，以减轻飞机重量。波音 737 MAX 10 已经面临多年严重的认证延迟。阿拉斯加还指出，将屏幕远离主舱有助于他们避免进一步复杂的硬件认证延迟，从而使飞机更快地升空。该航空公司指望免费的 Starlink WiFi 足以满足客户的需求，并且无需座椅靠背屏幕。

阿拉斯加的 MAX 10 计划包括四个客舱。极光套房 (Aurora Suites) 位于最前面，其次是其全新的、也是第一个真正的高级经济舱：Premium Reserve。其背后是豪华舱，这实际上只是腿部空间更大的经济舱。最后，还将有一个配备标准经济座位的主舱。据 Live And Let's Fly 报道，只有前两个客舱配备了松下 Astrova 系统的座椅靠背屏幕。高级舱和经济舱乘客将使用自己的设备。
下表详细列出了即将推出的 MAX 10 不同客舱级别之间的主要差异。极光套房在 737 机身上的出现也将是该航空公司首次在 737 机身上出现。值得注意的是，并非即将交付的 105 MAX 10 中的每架飞机都将配备相同的布局。阿拉斯加州表示至少有 25 个将采用这种安排进行配置。
据 APEX 称，阿拉斯加高管将高级体验定义为套房和高级储备舱，而主舱则与机队的其他部分类似。阿拉斯加的波音窄体客机从未提供内置娱乐功能，而从维珍美国航空继承的空客飞机在合并后也失去了内置娱乐功能。该航空公司预计首架 MAX 10 将于 2027 年第二季度交付，但平躺式座椅要到 2028 年才会安装。
美国联邦航空管理局于 10 月 20 日正式对波音 737 MAX 10 进行认证，扫清了多年延误后的最后障碍。现在，阿拉斯加预计将在 2027 年接收 22 架 MAX 10 飞机。为了尽快让这些飞机投入使用并避免进一步延误，第一批飞机将采用阿拉斯加标准的高密度国内客舱布局，拥有 188 个座位。

与阿拉斯加现有机队的其他飞机一样，这些 2027 架飞机的所有机队都将严格使用 BYOD。配备 Aurora Suite 的 25 架飞机将成为一支特殊的优质重型子机队。这是 2028 年的特定机队，将在飞机前部引入 19 英寸（48.26 厘米）和 16 英寸（40.64 厘米）4K 屏幕，同时保持飞机后部裸露。这次推迟是计划外的，因​​为阿拉斯加向公众公布该设计时并不知道这些座椅仍在等待美国联邦航空局的批准。
延误的主要原因是 FAA 对平躺高级座椅进行了严格的 16G 动态碰撞测试。传统座椅笔直向前，这使得管理碰撞冲击力相对可预测。单通道喷气式飞机上的平躺套房通常以一定角度安装。 FAA 需要进行广泛的雪橇测试，以证明以一定角度放置的人体可以承受 16 G 力的撞击，而不会撞到套房墙壁或遭受严重的颈部和脊柱创伤。
为了在碰撞过程中通过美国联邦航空局严格的头部伤害标准，倾斜的平躺套件将需要高度复杂的充气式安全带。美国联邦航空局还必须将整个机舱安装认证为单一系统。然后，美国联邦航空局必须进行检查，以确认这些结构不会阻塞飞机其余部分的紧急出口路径。座椅制造商通常需要 18 至 24 个月的时间来设计、测试和调整外壳材料以通过这些特定的冲击法规。
星链在夏威夷航空空客 A330 机队的成功部署成为阿拉斯加的概念验证。在檀香山宽体客机上启动的试点计划直接通知了公司领导，并使阿拉斯加航空集团有信心在即将推出的 737 MAX 10 的主舱中削减座椅靠背屏幕。
然而，《夏威夷之音》质疑这些数据能证明什么。夏威夷航空的旧屏幕已经过时，这使得使用率下降更难解读为对座椅靠背娱乐本身的判断。忽视老化显示器的乘客并不一定拒绝屏幕。这些数据可能只是与 Hawaiian 的硬件问题有关，而不是与座椅靠背 IFE 整体问题有关。
这些宽体飞机飞越太平洋，飞越世界上一些最偏僻的航线，完全依赖卫星覆盖。运营数据证明，Starlink 提供门到门、低延迟的宽带。一条穿越大片偏远海洋空域的航线的成功推出也表明，同样的覆盖范围在美国大陆上空应该是可靠的。
夏威夷基本上充当了小白鼠的角色。当可以使用免费的地面速度互联网时，很大一部分旅客会主动绕过航空公司的内置娱乐系统。 A330 数据还凸显了内置屏幕仍然很重要的领域：高端市场。支付顶级票价的乘客期望享受一价全包的豪华环境，而无需拿起手机。
阿拉斯加非常重视其机队中拥有相同的窄体客舱，以便在航班延误或取消时可以无缝更换飞机。由于他们当前的 737-800、737-900ER 和 MAX 9 完全无屏幕，因此如果发生飞机交换，仅在 MAX 10 的背面引入屏幕会造成高度不一致的乘客体验。尽管如此，这一总体战略仍存在一些警告。

title_en: Qantas' Airbus A380 Hides 12 Crew Bunks Under Economy, And Seat 70D Is Their 2nd Way Out
title_zh: 澳航空客 A380 在经济舱下隐藏 12 名机组人员铺位，70D 座位是他们的第二条出路
summary: Where exactly can the crew rest on an Airbus A380? Flying on a Qantas flight, you may notice that there is a missing seat, a spot that hides a secret.
summary_zh: 空客 A380 上的机组人员究竟可以在哪里休息？乘坐澳洲航空的航班时，您可能会注意到缺少一个座位，这个座位隐藏着一个秘密。
body_en: Qantas' Airbus A380 Hides 12 Crew Bunks Under Economy, And Seat 70D Is Their 2nd Way Out
Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

Passengers settling into the economy cabin on one of Qantas ' Airbus A380 superjumbos have no idea that sitting just a little way below them is a subterranean capsule hotel where the crew can get some well-needed rest. While hundreds of travelers recline across the main deck, up to 12 off-duty cabin crew members rest in a 12-berth module tucked inside the forward section of the aft cargo hold.

The hidden lower-deck compartment is one of the more unique parts of the A380 structure, but is also a part that brings a complex safety and engineering challenge regarding emergency egress on ultra-long-range sectors like Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport (SYD) to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX). The reason for this is that regulatory compliance means a secondary escape route is needed that bypasses the cargo hold entirely, giving birth to a unique seat-map anomaly centered around row 70.

When looking at the A380 from a structural point of view, the vertical ovoid fuselage cross-section of the A380 can be split into three distinct levels: an upper passenger deck, a main passenger deck, and a lower cargo and utility hold. Single-deck airliners generally have space for crew rest areas carved out above or below the passenger cabin, but because the A380 has two decks full of passengers, the positioning of these spaces had to be thought out carefully. Aircraft designers decided to use the expansive headroom in the forward section of the aft cargo area to install a modular, 12-berth cabin crew rest facility so revenue-generating seating space on the main passenger floor above was not sacrificed, as detailed in Simple Flying analysis.

Access to this underground sanctuary is restricted to a steep, narrow staircase hidden behind a locked door situated between rows 65 and 66 in the economy cabin. As noted in insights from Executive Traveller , the interior resembles a compact Japanese capsule hotel, featuring individual padded mattresses, sound-dampening curtains, personal reading lights, AC and USB power outlets, intercom handsets, and emergency oxygen masks.

The subterranean bunks are isolated from the main cargo bays by reinforced structural bulkheads and heavy thermal insulation. The air-conditioning system pumps fresh air independently through the module, which helps to maintain a controlled climate that shields resting crew members from the ambient temperatures and noise levels generated by underfloor cargo systems.

Under strict aviation safety regulations established by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency, specifically EASA Special Condition D-04 as analyzed by Global Travel Post , any below-deck or lower-fuselage crew compartment must feature at least two widely separated emergency evacuation routes. The issue is that a single entryway can become blocked by fire, smoke, or structural deformation during an emergency, so a secondary floor exit is legally mandatory on all lower-deck crew rest modules. The requirement means off-duty staff can evacuate directly upward into the main passenger cabin and not have to transit through unpressurized or fire-suppressed cargo holds.

The main access stairwell between rows 65 and 66 is considered the default entry and exit point during normal flight operations, while the secondary floor hatch provides an immediate backup path directly into the economy aisle. The idea is to route both escape paths directly into the inhabited passenger deck above so that sleeping crew members can have continuous access to cabin oxygen and fire suppression boundaries.

Aviation safety authorities strictly enforce these dual-egress requirements during aircraft certification trials to verify that a full crew shift can clear the module in seconds. Tests require off-duty flight attendants to evacuate the lower compartment under simulated zero-visibility and heavy smoke conditions, all to show that both the primary stairwell and secondary hatch are accessible during difficult cabin angles or structural shifts, as noted in Simple Flying analysis . Meeting these strict regulatory benchmarks is what guarantees that lower-deck crew rest modules achieve the same survival standards as standard main-deck cabin infrastructure.

The subterranean crew rest module beneath the economy floor serves exclusively cabin crew, so what does that mean for the pilots? Flight crews actually are given access to an entirely different layout. As detailed in the Janes Airbus A380 Technical Analysis , the superjumbo's immense forward upper deck houses a dedicated pilot rest facility located immediately behind the cockpit.

Down in the depths of the A380, cabin crew sleep in tightly stacked horizontal pods resembling a railway sleeper carriage, whereas A380 pilots benefit from a more spacious, separate rest room equipped with an armchair, full-length bunk, and isolated climate controls. The reason for this separation is the differing fatigue-management rules and crew complement sizes that exist on ultra-long-haul rotations.

It may seem rather counterintuitive to create two separate rest areas; after all, space is an incredibly valuable and scarce commodity on any airliner. Having distinct facilities for pilots and cabin crew actually helps maintain strict operational boundaries during long international sectors. The upper-deck pilot rest area gives flight captains immediate, private access to the flight deck, while the larger lower-deck module gives flight attendants a centralized space to take scheduled breaks without disturbing passengers.

Taking a look at seat maps for the Qantas A380, some may notice a rather peculiar omission in the economy cabin: Seat 70D does not exist. As explored in an analysis from Australian Frequent Flyer , seats 70E, 70F, and 70G are retained in the center block, and the space where 70D should sit is left entirely open as a solid floor panel. To most passengers, this is simply a comfort extra, but its omission does have its own unique purpose.

As documented in viral pilot walkthroughs highlighted by the Sydney Morning Herald , this missing seat designation conceals a spring-loaded emergency escape hatch. In the rare event of a lower-deck emergency where the main staircase is blocked, resting crew members can manually release the floor hatch from below, pushing upward into the cabin floor space near row 70 to evacuate directly into the aisle.

Of course, keeping an escape hatch visible would be a worrying sight for passengers seated anywhere near it. So, to keep the escape mechanism hidden during regular passenger operations, the hatch panel sits flush with the cabin floor and is covered by standard airline carpeting. Built-in quick-release latches allow off-duty flight attendants to pop the panel open from below without needing any tools or assistance from passengers above.
body_zh: 澳航空客 A380 在经济舱下隐藏 12 名机组人员铺位，70D 座位是他们的第二条出路
航空公司和机场管理毕业生、商业飞行员学生和商业航空作家。
入住澳洲航空一架空客 A380 超级客机经济舱的乘客并不知道，就在他们下方不远的地方是一家地下胶囊旅馆，机组人员可以在那里得到必要的休息。当数百名旅客斜靠在主甲板上时，多达 12 名下班的机组人员在位于后货舱前部的 12 个泊位模块中休息。
隐藏的下层甲板舱是 A380 结构中较为独特的部分之一，但也是悉尼金斯福德史密斯机场 (SYD) 至洛杉矶国际机场 (LAX) 等超远程航段的紧急出口带来复杂的安全和工程挑战的部分。其原因是，合规性意味着需要一条完全绕过货舱的辅助逃生路线，从而产生了以第 70 排为中心的独特座位图异常现象。

从结构角度来看 A380，A380 的垂直卵形机身横截面可分为三个不同的层次：上乘客甲板、主乘客甲板以及下货舱和公用设施舱。单层客机通常在客舱上方或下方留有供机组人员休息的空间，但由于 A380 有两层载满乘客的甲板，因此必须仔细考虑这些空间的位置。飞机设计师决定利用后货舱前部宽敞的净空来安装模块化的 12 个泊位的机组人员休息设施，这样就不会牺牲上方主乘客层的创收座位空间，如简单飞行分析中所述。
通往这个地下避难所的通道仅限于经济舱第 65 排和第 66 排之间的陡峭狭窄楼梯，该楼梯隐藏在上锁的门后面。正如《Executive Traveler》的见解所述，其内部类似于紧凑型日本胶囊酒店，配有独立软垫床垫、隔音窗帘、个人阅读灯、AC 和 USB 电源插座、对讲机和紧急氧气面罩。
地下铺位通过加固结构舱壁和重型隔热材料与主货舱隔离。空调系统通过模块独立泵送新鲜空气，这有助于维持受控气候，保护休息的船员免受环境温度和地板下货物系统产生的噪音水平的影响。
根据欧盟航空安全局制定的严格航空安全法规，特别是《环球旅行邮报》分析的 EASA 特殊条件 D-04，任何甲板下或机身下部的机组人员舱必须至少有两条相距较远的紧急疏散路线。问题是，在紧急情况下，单个入口可能会被火灾、烟雾或结构变形堵塞，因此法律规定所有下层甲板的船员休息模块必须设有二级出口。这一要求意味着下班的工作人员可以直接向上疏散到主客舱，而不必通过未加压或已灭火的货舱。
第 65 排和第 66 排之间的主通道楼梯间被视为正常航班运行期间的默认入口和出口点，而二楼舱口则提供直接进入经济通道的即时备用路径。这个想法是将两条逃生路径直接通向上方有人居住的乘客甲板，以便睡觉的机组人员可以持续进入机舱氧气和灭火边界。
航空安全当局在飞机认证试验期间严格执行这些双出口要求，以验证全体机组人员轮班可以在几秒钟内清除模块。测试要求下班的空乘人员在模拟零能见度和浓烟条件下疏散下层舱室，所有这些都是为了表明在困难的客舱角度或结构变化期间，主楼梯间和辅助舱口都可以进入，如简单飞行分析中所述。满足这些严格的监管基准可以保证下甲板船员休息模块达到与标准主甲板客舱基础设施相同的生存标准。
经济舱下方的地下机组休息舱专门为机组人员服务，那么这对飞行员意味着什么呢？实际上，机组人员可以使用完全不同的布局。正如《简氏空客 A380 技术分析》中详细介绍的那样，这架超级客机巨大的前上甲板在驾驶舱后面设有专门的飞行员休息设施。
在 A380 的深处，机组人员睡在紧密堆叠的水平舱内，类似于铁路卧铺车厢，而 A380 飞行员则受益于更宽敞、独立的休息室，配有扶手椅、全长铺位和独立的气候控制装置。造成这种分离的原因是超长途轮换中存在不同的疲劳管理规则和机组人员规模。
创建两个独立的休息区似乎相当违反直觉；毕竟，对于任何客机来说，空间都是极其宝贵且稀缺的商品。为飞行员和机组人员提供独特的设施实际上有助于在长途国际航段中保持严格的操作边界。上层甲板的飞行员休息区为机长提供了直接进入飞行甲板的私人通道，而较大的下层甲板模块为空乘人员提供了一个集中的空间，可以在不打扰乘客的情况下进行预定的休息。
看看澳洲航空 A380 的座位图，有些人可能会注意到经济舱中有一个相当奇怪的遗漏：70D 座位不存在。根据澳大利亚飞行常客的分析，70E、70F 和 70G 座位保留在中心区域，而 70D 应该坐的空间则完全开放，作为实心地板面板。对于大多数乘客来说，这只是一种额外的舒适感，但它的省略确实有其独特的目的。
正如《悉尼先驱晨报》所强调的病毒式飞行员演练中所记录的那样，这个缺失的座位名称隐藏了一个弹簧式紧急逃生舱口。在罕见的下层甲板紧急情况下，主楼梯被堵塞，休息的船员可以从下方手动释放地板舱口，向上推入第 70 排附近的客舱地板空间，直接撤离到过道。
当然，对于坐在逃生舱口附近的乘客来说，保持逃生舱口可见将是一个令人担忧的景象。因此，为了在常规乘客操作过程中保持逃生装置隐藏，舱口盖板与客舱地板齐平，并覆盖有标准的航空公司地毯。内置的快速释放闩锁允许下班的空乘人员从下方弹出面板，而不需要上方乘客的任何工具或帮助。

KLM’s first Airbus A350-900 has operated its inaugural passenger flight from Amsterdam Schiphol to Toronto. Named De Nachtwacht (“The Night Watch”), the aircraft departed as flight KL691 with passengers and eight tonnes of cargo aboard.

The inaugural attracted aviation enthusiasts who booked specifically for the occasion, including two passengers wearing specially printed T-shirts and a father and son who travelled from New York to join the flight.

The A350’s introduction forms part of KLM’s fleet-renewal programme, which the airline says aims to reduce fuel consumption, emissions and noise. Following Toronto, planned destinations for the aircraft include Montreal, Kilimanjaro, Dar es Salaam, Nairobi and Zanzibar.

title_en: The Airline With The World's Most Comfortable Premium Economy Seat
title_zh: 拥有全球最舒适高级经济舱座椅的航空公司
summary: A closer look at what Emirates has done to differentiate its premium economy cabin from the competition.
summary_zh: 仔细看看阿联酋航空为使其高端经济舱在竞争中脱颖而出所做的努力。
body_en: Daniel comes to Simple Flying with a business focused approach to the aviation world. Daniel enjoys analyzing strategy and how companies move against each other to gain a step ahead in the skies. Besides strategy, Daniel also has a passion for aircraft design and the history of aviation.

Initially, airlines offered just one cabin because flying itself was a luxury experience, and then first class emerged as a premium option. As first class seats became larger and more comfortable, business class emerged as a middle option, while innovations in economy mainly focused on space efficiency.

Eventually, business class seats became luxurious enough that first class was largely unnecessary for most airlines, but the growing space between business class and economy created demand for the new premium economy class. This has become extremely popular with passengers, and airlines around the world are increasingly introducing premium economy cabins to capitalize on growing demand.

Five years ago, Emirates announced that it, too, was throwing its hat in the ring and began operating flights with premium economy in 2022. The airline has experienced tremendous success and is adding the seats to most of its fleet, while the cabin has also been highly regarded as being one of, if not the best, premium economy experiences in the world. In terms of the seat itself, Skytrax ranks it first .

Emirates first announced premium economy in January 2021, and it first debuted the cabin on an Airbus A380 in May 2022. The A380s featured 56 seats configured eight abreast at the front of the main deck, and while large, the cabin size was fairly standard for the A380. The premium economy-equipped A380s initially flew to Emirates' highest-demand destinations such as London, Paris, and Sydney.

Meanwhile, the Boeing 777-300ER received premium economy later, with a fairly modest cabin consisting of 24 seats in an eight-abreast layout. In November 2024, Emirates began taking delivery of the Airbus A350-900, and all A350s have been delivered with premium economy.

Once again, the premium economy cabin is relatively small, with either 21 seats or 28 seats (depending on layout), and the seats are notably configured seven-abreast. Meanwhile, Emirates has also installed premium economy on its 777-200LRs, with the same configuration as the 777-300ER, and it has retrofitted all ten of its 777-200LRs.

In the future, the carrier plans to install premium economy on 110 of its A380s and 71 of its 777-300ERs, while also taking delivery of 73 A350-900s. In addition, Emirates holds an absolutely massive order for the Boeing 777X with 270 units in total, and all of these aircraft will include premium economy.

On paper, Emirates' premium economy seat isn't that special, especially considering that it's widely considered to be one of the world's top products in this space. Emirates uses the Recaro PL3530, a fairly standard seat model used by several airlines, and it lacks some features introduced by later seats.

There are no privacy dividers or wireless chargers, and while the 13.3-inch (33.78 cm) screen is good, it's the same size as the screen in economy, where Emirates has led the industry. The carrier differentiates itself with comfort elements rather than features . It configures its seats with 40 inches (101.6 cm) of pitch, rather than the standard 38 inches (96.52 cm).

The seat has eight inches (20.32 cm) of recline, among the best in the industry, and the seat features a calfrest as well as a footrest. The seat width of 19.5 inches (49.53 cm) is standard on the A380 and 777, but Emirates installs seven seats per row on the A350 rather than the standard eight, allowing it to maintain the same seat width.

At first, Emirates' premium economy essentially looks like a prettier version of every other airline's premium economy, but it's differentiating through adding more space and boosting comfort in subtle ways. As such, while the seat isn't as flashy as some newer seats with wireless charging, water bottle holders, 4K screens, and privacy wings, the seat is remarkably effective at providing a comfortable experience.

In the industry, the term 'hard product' typically refers to fixed parts of the aircraft that affect the passenger experience, mainly the seats. Meanwhile, 'soft product' refers to the more variable aspects of a flight, specifically the service, catering, and amenities. Here, Emirates shines because the carrier is already renowned for providing an excellent soft product in first class, business class, and economy.

Premium economy is no exception, with Emirates offering an industry-leading experience. Emirates' flight attendants are known for providing thoughtful, attentive service, and the smaller cabin size allows for more personal interactions between passengers and crew compared to economy.

In addition, passengers receive an amenity kit stocked with socks, an eye mask, earplugs, a Colgate dental kit, as well as lip balm, hand cream, and face lotion provided by Aveda. Then there's the catering, which is among the most thorough and elevated that you'll find in any premium economy cabin.
body_zh: Daniel 带着以商业为中心的方式进入航空界，加入了 Simple Flying。丹尼尔喜欢分析战略以及公司如何相互竞争以取得领先一步。除了战略之外，丹尼尔还对飞机设计和航空历史充满热情。
最初，航空公司只提供一个舱位，因为飞行本身就是一种奢侈的体验，然后头等舱成为一种优质选择。随着头等舱座位变得更大、更舒适，商务舱成为中间选择，而经济舱的创新主要集中在空间效率上。
最终，商务舱座位变得足够豪华，以至于大多数航空公司基本上不需要头等舱，但商务舱和经济舱之间不断扩大的空间创造了对新的高端经济舱的需求。这已变得非常受乘客欢迎，世界各地的航空公司越来越多地推出豪华经济舱，以满足不断增长的需求。
五年前，阿联酋航空宣布也将参与其中，并于 2022 年开始运营豪华经济舱航班。该航空公司取得了巨大的成功，并为其大部分机队增加了座位，而客舱也被高度认为是世界上最好的豪华经济舱体验之一。就座位本身而言，Skytrax 将其排名第一。
阿联酋航空于 2021 年 1 月首次推出高端经济舱，并于 2022 年 5 月在空客 A380 上首次推出该客舱。A380 设有 56 个座位，在主甲板前部并排 8 个座位，虽然宽敞，但客舱尺寸对于 A380 来说相当标准。配备高端经济舱的 A380 最初飞往阿联酋航空需求最高的目的地，如伦敦、巴黎和悉尼。
与此同时，波音 777-300ER 后来获得了高级经济舱，机舱相当朴素，共有 24 个座位，采用八并排布局。 2024年11月，阿联酋航空开始接收空客A350-900，所有A350均已交付豪华经济舱。

再次强调，豪华经济舱相对较小，有 21 个座位或 28 个座位（取决于布局），而且座位特别是七并排配置。与此同时，阿联酋航空还在其777-200LR上安装了豪华经济舱，其配置与777-300ER相同，并对其全部十架777-200LR进行了改装。
未来，该航空公司计划在 110 架 A380 飞机和 71 架 777-300ER 飞机上安装豪华经济舱，同时还将接收 73 架 A350-900 飞机。此外，阿联酋航空还持有波音777X的绝对巨额订单，总计270架，而且所有这些飞机都将包括豪华经济舱。
从纸面上看，阿联酋航空的高级经济舱座椅并没有那么特别，特别是考虑到它被广泛认为是该领域的世界顶级产品之一。阿联酋航空使用 Recaro PL3530，这是多家航空公司使用的相当标准的座椅型号，它缺少后来座椅引入的一些功能。
没有隐私隔板或无线充电器，虽然 13.3 英寸（33.78 厘米）的屏幕很好，但它与经济舱的屏幕尺寸相同，而阿联酋航空在经济舱中处于领先地位。该航空公司凭借舒适性元素而非特色而脱颖而出。其座椅间距配置为 40 英寸（101.6 厘米），而不是标准的 38 英寸（96.52 厘米）。
该座椅具有 8 英寸（20.32 厘米）的倾斜度，是业内最好的，并且座椅配有小腿托和脚踏板。 19.5 英寸（49.53 厘米）的座椅宽度是 A380 和 777 的标准座椅宽度，但阿联酋航空在 A350 上每排安装 7 个座椅，而不是标准的 8 个，使其保持相同的座椅宽度。
乍一看，阿联酋航空的高端经济舱本质上看起来就像其他航空公司的高端经济舱的更漂亮版本，但它通过增加更多空间并以微妙的方式提高舒适度来实现差异化。因此，虽然这款座椅不像一些带有无线充电、水瓶架、4K 屏幕和隐私翼的新型座椅那么华丽，但它在提供舒适体验方面非常有效。
在行业中，“硬产品”一词通常指飞机上影响乘客体验的固定部件，主要是座椅。同时，“软产品”是指航班中变化较多的方面，特别是服务、餐饮和便利设施。阿联酋航空在这方面大放异彩，因为该航空公司已经因在头等舱、商务舱和经济舱提供卓越的软产品而闻名。
豪华经济舱也不例外，阿联酋航空提供业界领先的体验。阿联酋航空的空乘人员以提供周到、周到的服务而闻名，与经济舱相比，较小的客舱面积允许乘客和机组人员之间进行更多的个人互动。
此外，乘客还可以获得一套洗漱用品，其中包括袜子、眼罩、耳塞、高露洁牙科套件，以及 Aveda 提供的润唇膏、护手霜和乳液。然后是餐饮，这是您在任何高级经济舱中都能找到的最彻底、最高档的餐饮。

body_en: Air Transat adds Geneva and Birmingham among five new European routes for summer 2027 - Aviation24.be
Air Transat has announced five new non-stop routes between Canada and Europe for summer 2027, including services to two new destinations: Geneva from Montreal and Birmingham from Toronto.
The Canadian leisure airline will also launch Quebec City–Lyon, Quebec City–Barcelona and Montreal–Faro services. The announced schedule is

Route Weekly flights Operating days Operating period in 2027 Montreal–Geneva 2 Tuesday, Saturday 19 June–23 October Toronto–Birmingham 2 Tuesday, Friday 22 June–22 October Quebec City–Lyon 1 Tuesday 8 June–26 October Quebec City–Barcelona 1 Monday 14 June–25 October Montreal–Faro 1 Monday 14 June–25 October

Birmingham will complement Air Transat’s existing London and Manchester services from Toronto. Faro, already served from Toronto, will become its third Portuguese destination from Montreal, alongside Lisbon and Porto.
The additions of Lyon and Barcelona will bring Air Transat’s non-stop European network from Quebec City to five destinations, joining Paris, Marseille and Nantes.
Meanwhile, Quebec City–Puerto Plata and Montreal–St Maarten will be extended to year-round operation, with one weekly summer flight on Mondays and Saturdays, respectively.
